name: C
summary: Portable systems programming language created at Bell Labs for Unix; a small, manually memory-managed, statically typed procedural language standardized by ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14 and the lingua franca of operating systems, runtimes and foreign-function interfaces.

level_notes.0: No reference implementation: GCC and Clang/LLVM are the dominant compilers; TinyCC, chibicc, lcc and cproc are small readable ones; CompCert is a formally verified compiler. The standard library is a separate project (glibc, musl, ...).
level_notes.1: The ISO/IEC 9899 standard is paywalled. The freely available WG14 working drafts are linked instead: N3220 (first draft after C23, practically identical to it), N1570 (C11) and N1256 (C99). Section deep links use the HTML rendering of N3220 hosted at port70.net, whose anchors are the standard's clause numbers.
level_notes.2: cppreference.com (a community-maintained reference that paraphrases the standard) is treated as level 2; it answers 403 to automated clients, so those links are reported as 'blocked' by the checker.
level_notes.3: Wikipedia has separate articles for syntax, data types, the standard library and each standard revision.
